reasoning: The problem asks for a graph on 24 vertices with girth at least 7, at least 33 edges, and colorable with at most 3 colors. The McGee graph is the unique 3-regular graph on 24 vertices with girth 7 (known as the (3,7)-cage). It has exactly (24 * 3) / 2 = 36 edges, which satisfies the edge count condition (36 >= 33). By Brooks' Theorem, any connected graph with a maximum degree of 3 is 3-colorable unless it is the complete graph K4. Since the McGee graph has a girth of 7, it is triangle-free and thus 3-colorable. We can construct the McGee graph by taking a 24-vertex cycle and adding 12 chords. To avoid creating any cycles of length 6 or less, the chords are chosen to connect vertices at a distance of 7 or 12 along the cycle, specifically shifted to maximize the distance between the endpoints of different chords.
